matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Changing orientation would produce a shape that does not correspond to any allowed Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you move a stick, verify that its orientation stays the same.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick and placing it vertically, turning a V into an I.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere. The total stick count must stay constant.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalising a move, ensure you have taken one stick and re‑attached it somewhere else.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral and not placing it elsewhere, reducing the total stick count.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every token must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a permitted operator (+, -, =). Invalid shapes break the puzzle rules.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each relocation, check that each symbol can be interpreted as a valid numeral or operator.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with only one diagonal stick, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds after the move. A visually plausible equation may still be numerically false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate corrected equation, compute both sides and confirm they are equal.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformed equation that still reads 15 = 10 without checking the numeric values.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, using uppercase letters and a single space between tokens. Any deviation causes a format mismatch.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, ensure the line follows the required exact format.
matchstick.example: Writing ‘Correct version of the equation: XV=XX-V’ without the required spaces and uppercase, causing a format error.

matchstick.title: Intra‑character V↔X transformation
matchstick.principle: To change a V into an X (or X into a V) while preserving stick count, reposition one of the character’s own diagonal sticks. This changes the value by ±5 and leaves the character valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the arithmetic difference is exactly 5, look for a V that can be turned into an X (or vice‑versa) by moving a diagonal within the same character.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from a V to another character, leaving the original V invalid, instead of repositioning it inside the V.

matchstick.title: Preserve exactly one equals sign
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one ‘=’ operator after the move; you cannot remove it or turn it into another symbol. The equals sign always consists of two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you consider moving a stick from the ‘=’ sign, make sure you replace it so that two horizontals remain.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal line from ‘=’, turning it into a single ‘-’, thus eliminating the equals sign.

matchstick.title: Target numeral based on arithmetic difference
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides, find the numeric difference, and identify a numeral that can be altered by a single‑stick move to adjust the total by that exact amount.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After calculating the difference, search for a numeral whose value can be increased or decreased by that amount using an allowed transformation.
matchstick.example: Changing a random numeral without considering the computed difference, resulting in an unbalanced equation.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain two diagonals, otherwise the character is no longer a legal numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you consider moving a diagonal from an X or V, ensure the source character still has two diagonals after the move.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from an X, leaving it with a single diagonal line, which is not a valid X.

matchstick.title: Preserve operator integrity
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick that belongs to an operator (+ or -), ensure the remaining sticks still form a recognized operator. A plus needs one vertical and one horizontal; a minus needs a single horizontal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before relocating a stick from a ‘+’ or ‘-’, verify that the operator will remain valid after the removal.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from ‘+’, turning it into ‘-’, and not compensating elsewhere, leaving an invalid operator configuration.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often focuses on moving sticks without checking whether the resulting equation actually balances.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a transformation, convert both sides to Arabic numbers and confirm equality before finalising the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may output the corrected equation but omit the required leading line or use wrong capitalization/spacing.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with a line exactly matching ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’, using uppercase letters and single spaces.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes a stick without placing it elsewhere, violating the one‑stick‑move rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the stick you move and ensure it is placed in a new location, keeping the total stick count unchanged.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick out of a numeral can leave it with too few sticks, producing a shape that is not a legal Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only move sticks that can be repositioned while leaving the original numeral still valid (e.g., intra‑character V↔X, or moving an entire I).

matchstick.description: Invalid operator after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes removes or alters essential sticks of a + or - sign, turning the operator into an undefined or different symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When relocating a stick from an operator, ensure the remaining sticks still form a recognized operator (+ requires one vertical and one horizontal; - requires one horizontal).
